## Summary

I'd like to introduce myself and offer concrete contributions to the WG's threat-taxonomy and design-pattern deliverables. Posting this as an issue because WG meetings are member-only — if there's a more appropriate public channel for non-member contributors, happy to redirect.

I am not affiliated with an AAIF member organization (I'm the founder of Ultra Lab, Taiwan); engagement here is as an individual contributor.

## What I'd offer the WG (three concrete deliverables)

Reading [`DRAFT-taxonomy.md`](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/main/deliverables/DRAFT-taxonomy.md), three places where my upstream work composes cleanly:

### 1. Agentic Threats — extend with OWASP ASI01-09 cross-reference

The current section has 6 terms (Agent derailment / sabotage / Blast radius / Multi-agent persuasion / Rogue agent / Typo squatting). The OWASP ASI (Agentic Systems Incidents) catalog formalized **9 vector families** that map directly into these terms but with finer granularity. The Microsoft AGT #3028 mapping I shipped last week:

| ASI ID | Vector | Maps to existing taxonomy term |
|---|---|---|
| ASI01 | Goal Hijacking | Agent sabotage |
| ASI02 | Scope Violation | Rogue agent / Agent derailment |
| ASI03 | Memory Poisoning | (gap — no current term) |
| ASI04 | Tool Misuse | Rogue agent (subset) |
| ASI05 | Identity Spoofing | (gap — see Identity section) |
| ASI06 | Resource Exhaustion | Blast radius (subset) |
| ASI07 | Authorization Bypass | (gap) |
| ASI08 | Cross-agent Trust Violation | Multi-agent persuasion (subset) |
| ASI09 | Supply Chain Compromise | Typo squatting (subset) |

Happy to PR a `### OWASP ASI Cross-Reference` subsection that bridges the WG taxonomy to the ASI catalog without breaking the WG's existing terms.

### 2. Security Practices — add "Static analysis" as a discipline distinct from red teaming

The current section has 3 terms (Hooks and checkpoints / Prompt injection / Red teaming). Static analysis is the layer in between — deterministic, zero-LLM, pre-execution, complementary to red teaming. Could contribute a term + a short design-pattern note: where in the agent lifecycle static analysis runs, what it catches that runtime detection misses, and what it does not (cannot reason about model behaviour).

### 3. Design Pattern — HITL implementation on consumer messaging surfaces

The taxonomy defines **Human in the loop (HITL)**. The WG charter scope includes "Security Architecture and Design Patterns". I can contribute a reference design pattern for HITL when the consumer surface is a messaging app (LINE/Telegram/WhatsApp/Slack rather than IDE-resident chat). Pin's preview/confirm runtime is a production implementation — covers preview rendering, confirmation token binding, idempotency, expiry, and the rate-limit/abuse-prevention layer. The pattern composes with capability tokens (per Identity & Authorization section) and Deterministic policies (per Agentic Controls).

## What I'd like to know

1. Is there a public PR/contributor pathway for non-member individuals? Happy to send PRs to `deliverables/` if that's the right shape, or open further issues if the WG prefers issues for early-stage proposals.
2. Is there a public observer / read-only attendance option for biweekly meetings? Understood that participation is member-only; not requesting attendance, just asking if recordings/transcripts go public after the fact.
3. Are there specific terms or sections in `DRAFT-taxonomy.md` where a PR right now would be welcome vs disruptive (the doc says "living"; I want to be helpful not noisy)?

Will defer to chairs on what's most useful to ship first. The PR contributions above are all artifacts I can produce within a week without WG meeting input — the question is which one is least premature given the WG's own roadmap.

cc/ @awfrazer @mindpower — apologies for the open ping; I couldn't find a less intrusive contact path for non-members. If preferred, I'm happy to take this to email instead (`support@aaif.io`?) and close this issue.

— Min Yi Hsieh / Ultra Lab (Taiwan)
